content.text: {"label":"unknown_demand_surge","explanation":"General queue volume jumped from about normal to +25% at 14:15 and +97% at 14:30, and service level fell to 16.9%. The excess is concentrated in login_issue calls (2.4x normal, about 55 extra calls), so it looks like a customer-facing login problem. Nothing confirms that: the only open incident is a P4 HR portal slowdown with no customer impact. The only marketing send was a newsletter at 09:10 with no call-to-action. Attendance is normal (2 sick on each queue, against about 2.2–2.4 usually). Without a confirmed cause this is an unknown demand surge. Payments looks broadly on plan, though it also dipped to 50% service level at 14:30.","plan_name":"General queue surge containment","rationale":"Add capacity to general quickly with the free levers first. Delay upcoming breaks and cancel non-mandatory coaching on general. Offer overtime for two hours from when agents can arrive (Rs 360 × about 4 accepting × 2 h ≈ Rs 2,880, well inside budget). Offer callbacks to callers facing waits over 120 s to flatten the peak. Deflect a share of simple balance and offer enquiries to chat (about Rs 12 per chat). I do not move cross-skilled agents from payments: it dropped to 50% service level at 14:30, so it may not stay at or above 70% as a donor. I do not use the outage message because no outage is confirmed.
